processing: Typical of Darjeeling: orthodox black tea, withered, rolled, oxidised and dried.
harvest_season: As across Darjeeling, first flush in spring and second flush from around May to June, followed by monsoon and autumn pickings.
appearance_dry: Twisted Darjeeling leaf in mixed olive and brown, as usual for the region.
appearance_liquor: Gold to amber, depending on the flush.
taste_profile: Few tasting records name this garden. Expect the general Darjeeling pattern: floral and brisk in spring, fruitier and fuller in summer.

brewing.notes: Brewed Western-style, as for other Darjeeling. Use cooler water and a shorter steep for first flush.

vintage_note: As usual for Darjeeling, expect it sold by year and flush. Little is recorded about this garden's own lots, so ask the seller for both and prefer the latest harvest.
description:
Longview is a Kurseong garden whose story is mostly about the company that carried its name. The Longview Tea Company grew from this one garden into a group across Darjeeling, the Dooars and the Terai before selling most of it off.

The making is presumably the usual orthodox Darjeeling process; little has been written about the garden's own methods or how they changed under new owners.

In the cup, expect the regional seasons: light and floral first flush, rounder second flush. That is general Darjeeling guidance rather than a note on this particular garden.

As with any lesser-known estate, buy small and buy recent. The year and flush on the label matter more here than the name.
history:
Accounts differ on the start. The Longview Tea Company was incorporated in 1879, while another account says the British planter C. G. Adams opened the estate in 1873. James Warren and Company is also named among its early owners, and Wyandhams of Australia are said to have held it until 1953.

The Daga family took over the company in 1954, and it went on to acquire Phuguri, Bhatpara, Orange Valley, Sanyasithan and Anandapur. It later sold Longview itself to Ambari Tea, leaving Orange Valley as its only Darjeeling garden by 2000.
